Rule.Name: Establish Backup Policy (Automated)
Rule.Section: Backup and Disaster Recovery - Establish Backup Policy
Rule.NonCompliantComment: No backup policy is defined, which may result in data loss.
Rule.CorrectiveComment: Establish a backup policy for MariaDB databases, including full, incremental, and transaction log backups.
Rule.Correction: echo 'Backup policy: Daily full backup, hourly incremental backups, and transaction log backups.' > /etc/mysql/backup_policy.txt

Rule.Name: Verify Backups Regularly (Automated)
Rule.Section: Backup and Disaster Recovery - Verify Backups Regularly
Rule.NonCompliantComment: Backups are not verified, which may result in unreliable recoveries.
Rule.CorrectiveComment: Regularly verify backups by performing test restores using valid SQL dump files.

Rule.Name: Secure Backup Credentials (Automated)
Rule.Section: Backup and Disaster Recovery - Secure Backup Credentials
Rule.NonCompliantComment: Backup credentials are stored in plain text, which may expose them to unauthorized users.
Rule.CorrectiveComment: Secure backup credentials by storing them in a secure vault or encrypting them.

Rule.Name: Secure Backup Directories (Automated)
Rule.Section: Backup and Disaster Recovery - Secure Backup Directories
Rule.NonCompliantComment: Backups are not properly secured, making them vulnerable to unauthorized access.
Rule.CorrectiveComment: Ensure backup directories are secured with appropriate permissions.

Rule.Name: Enable Point-in-Time Recovery (Automated)
Rule.Section: Backup and Disaster Recovery - Enable Point-in-Time Recovery
Rule.NonCompliantComment: Point-in-Time Recovery (PITR) is not enabled, which may prevent restoring to a specific point in time.
Rule.CorrectiveComment: Enable binary logging to allow point-in-time recovery.
Rule.Correction: grep -Eq '^\s*log_bin' /etc/mysql/my.cnf || (grep -q '^\[mysqld\]' /etc/mysql/my.cnf && sed -i '/^\[mysqld\]/a log_bin' /etc/mysql/my.cnf || echo -e '[mysqld]\nlog_bin' >> /etc/mysql/my.cnf); mysqladmin shutdown; mysqld_safe --skip-syslog &

Rule.Name: Establish Disaster Recovery Plan (Automated)
Rule.Section: Backup and Disaster Recovery - Establish Disaster Recovery Plan
Rule.NonCompliantComment: No Disaster Recovery (DR) plan is defined, which may result in prolonged downtime during an incident.
Rule.CorrectiveComment: Establish a Disaster Recovery (DR) plan for MariaDB, including replication and failover procedures.
Rule.Correction: echo 'Disaster Recovery Plan: Backup, Replication, Failover' > /etc/mysql/dr_plan.txt

Rule.Name: Backup Configuration Files (Automated)
Rule.Section: Backup and Disaster Recovery - Backup Configuration Files
Rule.NonCompliantComment: Configuration and related files are not backed up, which may result in misconfiguration after recovery.
Rule.CorrectiveComment: Regularly backup configuration files, including my.cnf and user configuration files.

Rule.Name: Dedicated Server for MariaDB (Automated)
Rule.NonCompliantComment: MariaDB is installed on a multi-use server, increasing security risks.
Rule.CorrectiveComment: Dedicate the server exclusively to MariaDB.
Rule.Correction: systemctl stop apache2; systemctl disable apache2

Rule.Name: Do Not Use Command Line Passwords (Automated)
Rule.Section: Do Not Use Command Line Passwords
Rule.NonCompliantComment: Passwords are specified in the command line, exposing them to unauthorized users.
Rule.CorrectiveComment: Use secure password files or environment variables for authentication.

Rule.Name: Ensure Unique Usernames (Automated)
Rule.NonCompliantComment: Usernames are reused, which can lead to confusion and security risks.
Rule.CorrectiveComment: Ensure usernames are unique and not reused.
Rule.Verification: mysql -e "SELECT user FROM mysql.user GROUP BY user HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;" | grep -q . && echo 1 || echo 0

Rule.Name: Use Strong Cryptographic Material for SSL/TLS (Automated)
Rule.Section: Use Strong Cryptographic Material for SSL/TLS
Rule.NonCompliantComment: Default or weak cryptographic material is used, reducing security.
Rule.CorrectiveComment: Ensure unique, strong cryptographic material is used for SSL/TLS.

Rule.Name: Set Password Lifetime (Automated)
Rule.NonCompliantComment: The 'password_lifetime' parameter is not configured, allowing passwords to never expire.
Rule.CorrectiveComment: Set 'password_lifetime' to a value less than or equal to 365 days.
Rule.Verification: mysql -e "SHOW VARIABLES LIKE 'password_lifetime';" | grep -q '365' && echo 0 || echo 1

Rule.Name: Lock Inactive Accounts (Automated)
Rule.NonCompliantComment: Inactive accounts are not locked, increasing security risks.
Rule.CorrectiveComment: Lock inactive accounts to prevent unauthorized access.
Rule.Verification: mysql -e "SELECT user,host,account_locked FROM mysql.user WHERE account_locked='Y';" | grep -q 'Y' && echo 0 || echo 1

Rule.Name: Enable Socket Peer-Credential Authentication (Automated)
Rule.NonCompliantComment: Socket peer-credential authentication is not used, which may reduce security.
Rule.CorrectiveComment: Enable socket peer-credential authentication for secure local connections.
Rule.Verification: mysql -e "SHOW VARIABLES LIKE 'skip_name_resolve';" | grep -q 'ON' && echo 0 || echo 1

Rule.Name: Bind MariaDB to Specific IP Addresses (Automated)
Rule.Section: Bind MariaDB to Specific IP Addresses
Rule.NonCompliantComment: MariaDB is not bound to specific IP addresses, increasing exposure.
Rule.CorrectiveComment: Restrict MariaDB to one or more specific IP addresses (e.g., 127.0.0.1).
Rule.Verification: mysql -e "SHOW VARIABLES LIKE 'bind_address';" | grep -q '127.0.0.1' && echo 0 || echo 1

Rule.Name: Restrict TLS Versions (Automated)
Rule.NonCompliantComment: All TLS versions are enabled, increasing the risk of using weak versions.
Rule.CorrectiveComment: Restrict TLS to versions 1.2 and 1.3 only.
Rule.Verification: mysql -e "SHOW VARIABLES LIKE 'tls_version';" | grep -q 'TLSv1.2,TLSv1.3' && echo 0 || echo 1

Rule.Name: Require Client-Side Certificates (Automated)
Rule.NonCompliantComment: Client-side certificates are not required, which may allow unauthorized connections.
Rule.CorrectiveComment: Require client-side certificates (X.509) for secure connections.
Rule.Verification: mysql -e "SHOW VARIABLES LIKE 'require_secure_transport';" | grep -q 'ON' && echo 0 || echo 1

Rule.Name: Use Strong SSL/TLS Ciphers (Automated)
Rule.NonCompliantComment: Weak ciphers are enabled, increasing the risk of exploitation.
Rule.CorrectiveComment: Ensure only approved, strong ciphers are used for SSL/TLS.
Rule.Verification: mysql -e "SHOW VARIABLES LIKE 'ssl_ciphers';" | grep -q 'ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256' && echo 0 || echo 1
